# email-template-workflows

> A reusable GitHub composite Action (`LLazyEmail/email-template-workflows@v1`) that installs a Node.js consumer package, renders email templates to static HTML, uploads the HTML directory as a workflow artifact with a browsable `index.html`, and on pull requests posts or updates a single "Rendered emails" comment.

Use this Action when a repository builds HTML emails with an npm script or a CLI (MJML, Lit, Markdown-to-email, a template catalog) and you want CI to render them, publish them for review, and link them from the pull request. It is not an email sender, a linter, or a template library. It runs your build and publishes the result.

Pin to the floating major tag `@v1`. It tracks the latest `v1.x` release. Minimal call:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v7
- uses: LLazyEmail/email-template-workflows@v1
  with:
    working-directory: .
    command: npx generate-template --all --out=generated
    artifact-directory: generated
```

## Pick a render mode

- Script mode: set `input` + `output`, or a multiline `templates` (`input:output` per line). The Action runs `npm run <build-script> -- --input X --output Y [extra-args]` for each pair. Your script must accept `--input` and `--output`.
- Command mode: set `command` and `artifact-directory`. The Action runs the shell command as-is (no flags appended) and indexes the top-level `*.html` files in `artifact-directory`. `command` overrides `templates`, `input`, `output`, `build-script`, `validate-script`, and `extra-args`.

- [Real-world walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LLazyEmail/email-template-workflows/main/docs/real-world-example.md): explains the consumer workflow above line by line
